findings.summary: The gate only ever looks at files whose name ends in `.jar` (`dependencies.files.filter { it.name.endsWith(".jar") }`, twice, plus a `.sha1`-only sweep of licenses/). Any other artifact type resolved into the build -- a distribution `zip`, a `tar.gz`, a native `.so`/`.exe` classifier artifact -- is skipped with no pin, no licence, and no message. Unlike the literal-coordinate hole on build.gradle.kts:22-26, this one is not documented anywhere.
findings.failure_scenario: M0.16 adds the cluster-test tier and the catalogue gains an OpenSearch distribution archive, e.g. `opensearch-dist = { module = "org.opensearch.distribution:opensearch", version = "3.8.0" }` consumed as `@zip`. `licenseCheck` resolves it, the task's two filters drop it, the unused-sha sweep never mentions it because it only inspects `*.sha1` files, and `./gradlew dependencyLicenses` prints `ok 10 jar(s)` -- a green gate for a build that now pulls a multi-hundred-megabyte artifact nobody pinned or licensed. Either fail loudly on a non-jar entry (`problems += "unhandled artifact type ..."`) or state the jar-only assumption next to the catalogue-only one.

findings.summary: The denied-licence error tells the operator to "record an exception in baselines/licenses.txt" (build.md rule 3 says the same). Nothing reads that file: `baselines/` contains only `review.txt`, and neither the task nor scripts/check-dependency-licenses.sh mentions it outside the message text. The one instruction the message gives is inert.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified by executing the path: setting `junit  GPL-2.0-only` in licenses/SPDX.txt fails the task with seven copies of this message. An operator who does exactly what it says -- creates baselines/licenses.txt naming the dependency, the licence and the reviewer -- re-runs and gets the identical failure with no hint why. The only remaining way to proceed is to delete the identifier from the `denied` set in build.gradle.kts, i.e. weaken the gate to make the check pass, which is precisely AGENTS.md non-negotiable 2. Either implement the baseline read (the file exists, is staged, and lists `<prefix> <SPDX-ID> <reviewer>`) or drop the sentence and say the dependency must be replaced.

findings.summary: 252 lines of enforcement logic (deny-list, sha comparison, prefixFor, the unused-pin and unused-prefix sweeps) with no test anywhere -- `grep -rl DependencyLicenses` outside the two source files finds only build.gradle.kts, build.md and review-lenses.sh. buildSrc/build.gradle.kts:8 claims "buildSrc holds real logic now ... so it gets tests like anything else", but the only buildSrc test is JavaTestParserTest, which constrains the parser. check-tdd.sh scans Java `@Test` declarations, so Kotlin gate logic is the one place the TDD gate cannot see; check-harness-tests.sh only requires the suite to report >0 tests, which the parser fixtures already satisfy.
findings.failure_scenario: Named surviving mutations, all of which leave `./gradlew -p buildSrc test` green, `./gradlew build` green and the task printing `ok 10 jar(s)`: (a) delete `denied.set(...)` from build.gradle.kts -- `denied` is a managed SetProperty whose default is the empty set, not an error, so every licence is accepted; (b) change `else if (spdx in denied.get())` to `if (false)`; (c) make `sha1()` return `expected`; (d) drop the `problems.isNotEmpty()` throw. Each is a gate that reports success while checking nothing, and nothing in the tree would notice. A `DependencyLicensesTaskTest` driving the action over a temp `licenses/` directory (one denied case, one sha-mismatch case, one missing-pin case) is a handful of assertions and would kill all four; today only an agent re-deriving them by hand does, once.

findings.summary: Every 200 KB test jar carries a committed SHA-1 pin, but the Gradle distribution -- the largest artifact entering this build and the one that executes with the developer's full privileges -- is fetched from `distributionUrl` with no `distributionSha256Sum`. `validateDistributionUrl=true` validates the URL, not the bytes it returns. OpenSearch, whose licence mechanism this change deliberately models, does pin it.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor or CI runner with a poisoned DNS/proxy, or a future PR that edits `distributionUrl` to a look-alike host, downloads a modified gradle-9.7.0-bin.zip into ~/.gradle/wrapper/dists. Nothing compares it to anything: the build runs attacker-controlled code before any gate in this repository executes, including the licence gate itself, and `./gradlew build` is green. With the pin present the wrapper aborts with a checksum mismatch. The fix is one line, obtainable with `./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version 9.7.0 --gradle-distribution-sha256-sum <sum>`; the same follow-up should cover verification of the committed gradle-wrapper.jar, which no gate inspects either.
